tasks.task: Build a staff newsletter edition

items.when: When you have the month's news, leaders' notes and site updates and need the full edition
When the newsletter runs every week and each issue should be drafted, edited and scored the same way
Before sending, to get subject lines in several angles that earn the open and stay clear
When the lead story needs a headline and the first try reads like a notice board
When you have two or three lead stories or subject lines and want a fresh reader to pick
When the edition is drafted, to get cuts, a pacing map and a score before it goes out
When an item has no focus and the reader cannot tell why it matters to them

tasks.task: Write a leadership update in the leader's own voice

items.when: When a leader hands you rough notes and the update must sound like them and explain why
When the update and the town hall script are needed together from the same notes
When the update carries bad news and must be pitched to one named audience
Before each update goes out, to check it against the leader's voice and track repeat slips
Before sending, to have a fresh reader go through it as a staff member and list what rings false
When the draft hides the real news behind vague labels and padding

tasks.task: Capture a leader's voice so drafts sound like them

items.when: When you have the leader's past emails and talks and want a voice guide and a checked draft
When the best source is call transcripts and you need rules, examples and open questions
When the leader would rather talk than write, to get a transcript you can draft from

tasks.task: Write a town hall script and question bank

items.when: When a town hall is on the calendar and you need the steps from agenda to follow-up
When you need a timed script with honest answers, including what is not yet known
When leaders need answers ready for the questions staff will really ask, hardest first
When the room is angry, to try a version that agrees first and then turns step by step
When the script reads well on paper but must be heard, with a line people repeat
When the answers are drafted, to test them against the toughest pushback and admit the limits
When the talk is all numbers and needs one true incident people will remember

tasks.task: Write up a town hall with answers and actions

items.when: When you have rough notes and need decisions, actions with owners and open questions
When the session was recorded and you need the questions asked word for word
A week or two later, to see whether staff understood and know where to ask

tasks.task: Plan and write the full message set for big news

items.when: When a decision staff will feel is coming and you need who hears what, in what order
When you write the manager briefing, the message to affected staff and the all-staff note
Before drafting, to sort the affected groups and how to talk to each
When the leader also needs a town hall script and answers to the hard questions
When the change is a new direction, to try a memo-first route with listening talks
When each audience has its own version, to find where the versions contradict each other
When the message lists what changes but not who it helps or what protects trust

tasks.task: Write a manager briefing pack before an announcement

items.when: When managers will be asked about the news and must hear it first
When you need talking points, a FAQ and a rollout order alongside the announcement
When the pack is drafted, to list the hard questions teams will ask and grade each answer

tasks.task: Write messages for a restructure or job losses

items.when: When cuts are decided and you need a decision check, a manager script and the company note
Before anything is announced, to check services stay covered and who escalates
When you need the announcement, FAQ and a send plan for a re-org
When affected staff must hear in person before the all-staff message
Before sending, to read each message as someone who may lose their job
When the draft starts with the company and not with the people affected

tasks.task: Write a short announcement for Slack or Teams

items.when: When staff should be able to act on a chat post without opening anything else
When the first line decides if anyone reads on, to get several opening angles
Before posting, to cut the post to plain words and one action

tasks.task: Explain a new policy to staff with a FAQ

items.when: When a policy is approved and staff need a plain explanation and a rollout list
When staff keep asking the same things, to try the explainer as questions and answers
When the FAQ avoids the awkward questions staff will ask anyway
Before sending, to check every line matches the approved policy text

tasks.task: Rebuild an intranet page map around staff tasks

items.when: When the intranet follows the org chart and staff cannot find answers
When you have the page list and must mark each keep, update, merge or delete
When the new structure needs a hierarchy, navigation and a link plan written out
When the home page is being redone, to see three different first screens as real pages
When the menu labels are drafted, to score each choice and rewrite the unclear ones
When staff should get checked answers inside Slack or Teams instead of opening the intranet
When the intranet lives in Notion and pages are drafted and kept there

tasks.task: Rewrite an intranet page around the staff question

items.when: When a page is long or out of date and staff still email to ask the same thing
When you hold the real questions staff send, to try the page as questions and answers
When a form or process page uses the department's words, not the words staff say
When the page is a how-to and should be searchable with clear steps
When the answer sits in a chat thread and must become a linked wiki page
When you review a set of pages, to find stale ones and pages with no owner

tasks.task: Plan the internal comms calendar and monthly cycle

items.when: At the start of each month, to set what goes out, on which channel and who signs it off
When one internal campaign needs a brief with audience, messages, channels and a weekly plan
When you need to see which groups hear too much and which hear nothing

tasks.task: Plan the messages for a new tool or process rollout

items.when: When a tool switch needs a rollout plan, message templates and a plan for pushback
When the people side needs a stakeholder map, a message plan and adoption checks
Before launch day, to list open blockers and record the go or no-go decision

tasks.task: Run a pulse check after big news and reply to staff

items.when: One to two weeks after an announcement, to test whether staff understood it
When three questions are not enough and you need a focus group guide and a way to read results
When comments are in and each theme needs an owner and a reply to staff
Each month after, to draft the staff update on what was done and what is overdue

tasks.task: Report whether messages landed and what to change

items.when: When you must show if staff follow a change and name what gets in the way
When survey results are in, to see which answers you can trust
When leaders need one page with the answer first and the decision needed
When the report lists activity and never answers the question leaders asked

tasks.task: Write staff updates during a crisis or incident

items.when: When something has gone wrong and you need a first-hour staff message and a 24-hour list
When the facts are known and you need a clear incident note in a set format
Before each update, to separate what is confirmed from what is still a guess
When the update must start with affected people, known facts and named owners

tasks.task: Write a culture, values or priority memo

items.when: When a leader wants how the team should work written down in one short memo
When the top priority has changed and each area needs one stop and one start
When the memo is drafted, to find the pushback it will get and answer it fairly
When the values read like a poster and say nothing a person could act on

tasks.task: Write a people story or team spotlight

items.when: When the story will run in the newsletter and must fit its length and tone
When the story needs a headline that is about the person, not their job title
Before it runs, to fix names, titles and slips while keeping the person's own words
When the profile is a list of duties and needs one moment that shows who they are

tasks.task: Edit and proof a leader's or colleague's draft

items.when: When a draft is full of management words and each cut should be explained to its author
When the text must come back corrected in the writer's voice with a log of changes
When the draft has good material in the wrong order

tasks.task: Draft the slides for a town hall or leadership update

items.when: When the script is agreed and you need simple slides with speaker notes fast
When the leader's team wants a deck draft they can edit themselves
Before the session, to view the deck as someone at the back of the room would

tasks.task: Adapt one message for sites, shifts and languages

items.when: When part of the workforce reads another language and the tone must stay natural
When each site gets its own version, to make sure no two versions disagree
Before translating, to cut idioms and head-office terms that do not travel

always.when: At the start of any sizeable job, to capture the real firm, its sites and its channels first
Before anything reaches staff, to cut it to plain words they would say themselves
Whenever a message states dates, numbers or decisions, to tie each to an approved source

helpers.when: When a leader needs a full keynote or a hard speech, not a short script
When the town hall needs designed slides, not a quick draft
When the news changes a policy, a contract term or someone's job
When a pulse check shows a deeper problem that needs a proper survey and action plan
When the announcement depends on a restructure that is not yet designed
When the leader's message should go out as a short video

gaps: No library item builds an internal comms calendar or a channel plan that says which channel does which job
No library item writes a staff newsletter; the newsletter items are for customers or donors
No library item makes two or three clearly different versions of a leadership update, crisis update or restructure message to choose between
No library item plans the interview for a staff profile or writes a people story with consent
No library item reports internal comms reach, such as open and read rates by site or team
No library item plans how to reach frontline staff who have no work email or desk
No library item writes a script for a short leader video message
No library item makes different slide directions for a town hall deck
No library item sets intranet page owners and review dates beyond the kit skill
No library item plans a staff recognition programme or shout-out format
The library has no tool guide for Slack, Teams, SharePoint or a staff comms platform
